---
title: "Read the audit reports"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r build-reports, include=FALSE}
root <- rprojroot::find_package_root_file()
source_dir <- tempfile("distortions-")
dir.create(file.path(source_dir, "evidence", "benchmarks"), recursive = TRUE)
manifest <- read.csv(file.path(root, "inst", "examples", "distortions-source.csv"))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(manifest))) {
  file <- file.path(source_dir, "evidence", "benchmarks", manifest$file[i])
  download.file(manifest$url[i], file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  stopifnot(identical(digest::digest(file = file, algo = "sha256"), manifest$sha256[i]))
}
withr::with_envvar(c(DP_DATA_ROOT = source_dir), {
  withr::with_dir(root, source("inst/examples/gallery.R"))
})
destination <- file.path(root, "docs", "reports")
dir.create(destination, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
reports <- list.files(
  file.path(root, "artifacts", "gallery"), pattern = "\\.html$", full.names = TRUE
)
stopifnot(file.copy(reports, destination, overwrite = TRUE))
unlink(source_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

The reports below are complete rendered audits. Open a report to explore the
figures, filter diagnostics, inspect denominators and export table rows.

| Report | What to look for |
|---|---|
| [Balanced synthetic discussion](../reports/balanced.html) | Distributed participation and complete recording, under an illustrative policy |
| [Concentrated synthetic discussion](../reports/concentrated.html) | One participant takes the recorded participant turns, while opinions move and knowledge does not improve |
| [Incomplete synthetic recording](../reports/incomplete.html) | Missing recording coverage prevents a complete-session silence verdict |
| [Real data: distortions, paired respondents](../reports/distortions.html) | Item-specific learning, opinion change, response coverage and H/P/D across polls |
| [Real data: available-wave sensitivity](../reports/distortions-available.html) | How results differ when each wave uses all observed respondents |

Synthetic statements, participants and annotations are invented. The policy
thresholds demonstrate software behavior; they are not a validated standard for
judging deliberation. The real data supply surveys and group labels, so the
report leaves transcript and briefing diagnostics unavailable.

## Reproduce the reports

From the development repository, with deliberately installed:

```sh
Rscript inst/examples/gallery.R ../dp-data
```

This writes standalone HTML reports and audit R objects to `artifacts/gallery`.
The real-data import reads the frozen `polardata.tab` and `attitude-indices.tab`
benchmarks from [dp-data](https://github.com/soodoku/dp-data), under
`evidence/benchmarks/`. The bundled source manifest pins their revision and hashes.
Source files are hashed; exact duplicate removal and endpoint rounding are logged.
No participant data are bundled with this package.

The documentation website serves only aggregate HTML reports. The saved R objects
retain evidence and identifiers and belong in the research workspace.

## Read a report in order

Start with the findings and plots, then check response and recording coverage.
Use the diagnostic explorer to inspect an event, item, subgroup or method. Read
its denominator and assumptions before interpreting the estimate. Policy verdicts
follow the declared rules; missing inputs never create a PASS.

A large opinion change can coexist with poor process evidence, and almost no
opinion change can coexist with thoughtful discussion. Read participation,
argument consideration and learning together rather than treating movement as a
success criterion. The [design review](design-review.html) explains the limits of
each claim and the evidence needed to support stronger conclusions.
